hero.title: Phnom Penh Night Market
hero.subtitle: Set along the Tonle Sap riverfront, the Phnom Penh Night Market is a lively evening gathering place where locals and visitors browse stalls, enjoy street food, and experience the city's nightlife.

quickFacts.title: Quick Facts
quickFacts.intro: The essentials at a glance before you plan your visit.
quickFacts.note: The market is closed Monday – Thursday. It is an evening event, so stalls only start to open from around 5 PM. Hours may shift on public holidays — please confirm before you go. (Schedule checked October 2026.)

intro.title: About Phnom Penh Night Market
body: The Phnom Penh Night Market (Khmer: ផ្សាររាត្រី ភ្នំពេញ) is an open-air evening market located on the riverfront along Preah Sisowath Quay, near the junction with Street 106 in central Phnom Penh, Cambodia.

On Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings, as the sun sets, vendors set up stalls selling clothing, accessories, handicrafts, and souvenirs, while a large food section offers grilled dishes, noodles, and drinks beside the river.
More than a shopping spot, the market reflects everyday urban life in Cambodia's capital — a relaxed place where residents wind down and visitors get a feel for local culture after dark.

culture.title: History & Culture
body: Night markets are a long-standing part of urban life across Cambodia and Southeast Asia. Phnom Penh's riverside night market grew as the city's waterfront — near the confluence of the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers — became a focal point for public life after sunset, where cool river breezes have drawn residents to gather at dusk for generations.

Its signature is the open-air 'mat dining' tradition: the central plaza is laid with woven reed mats, and locals buy food from the stalls, slip off their shoes, and sit cross-legged with family and friends to share a meal — a living echo of rural Khmer communal feasting unique among Southeast Asian night markets.
Far from a tourist-only spectacle, Phsar Reatrey (ផ្សាររាត្រី ភ្នំពេញ) is where everyday Khmer life, handicraft heritage, and the modern city rhythm meet beside the water.

glossary.title: Khmer Language Mini-Guide
glossary.intro: A quick key to the local names you'll see around the market.

shopping.title: Shopping Experience
shopping.intro: Stroll through rows of stalls offering a mix of local and regional goods — look for these quintessential Khmer symbols.

items.title: Krama (ក្រមា)
items.desc: The iconic checkered cotton scarf with centuries of history — worn as a scarf, sun-shade, or all-purpose utility cloth in daily Khmer life.

items.title: Silver & Woodcarving
items.desc: Handmade silver jewelry and miniature red-ebony carvings inspired by Angkorian sculpture.

items.title: Silk & Textiles
items.desc: Handwoven scarves and silk products from Khmer weavers.

items.title: Souvenirs
items.desc: Postcards, magnets, and small keepsakes to remember your trip.

notes.stalls: Stalls are grouped roughly by type — clothing and accessories, handicrafts and silver, and souvenirs and gifts, with a dedicated street-food zone along the river.
notes.bargain: Haggling is normal and welcome at the market — keep it friendly. Most stalls take cash (USD or KHR); small purchases are easiest in riel or $1/$5 notes. Larger shops may accept card, ABA Pay or QR-code payment, but never assume it — carry some cash.

food.title: Top Street Food to Try at Phnom Penh Night Market
food.intro: The food court near the riverbank serves the most authentic Khmer home flavors — here are the dishes worth seeking out by name.

items.title: Sach Ko Yak (សាច់គោយ៉ាក់)
items.desc: Herbal grilled beef skewers marinated in lemongrass, turmeric, and kaffir lime leaf, charred over charcoal for a distinctly Southeast Asian aroma.

items.title: Lort Cha (ឆាចាប់)
items.desc: Short silver-pin noodles flash-fried with bean sprouts, chives, and egg, finished with a sweet-chili sauce — a favorite late-night energy boost.

items.title: Num Banh Chok (នំបញ្ចុក)
items.desc: Cambodia's national rice-noodle dish in a fragrant fish-curry broth, topped with fresh herbs and banana blossom.

items.title: Kuy Teav (គុយទាវ)
items.desc: Clear pork-bone broth simmered for hours, served with thin rice noodles, herbs, and beef or seafood.

items.title: Sugarcane & Kumquat Juice
items.desc: Fresh-pressed sugarcane juice with a squeeze of kumquat — sweet with a tangy lift, the classic way to cool off.

items.title: Around 17:00
items.desc: Stalls begin to open and the temperature eases after the afternoon heat.
Best atmosphere with full lighting, more vendors, and lively crowds.

items.title: Avoid Midday
items.desc: The market is an evening event; visiting at noon means little is open.

transport.title: How to Get to the Night Market
transport.intro: The market runs along Preah Sisowath Quay on the riverside. Below is how to reach it by each mode of transport, with rough times and costs.
transport.costNote: Times and fares are rough ranges only — they swing with traffic, time of night and negotiation.

modes.title: On Foot
modes.from: Sisowath Quay, Royal Palace, riverside hotels
points: Follow the riverside promenade — the pavement is even and lit, and it stays busy in the evening.
Roughly 15–20 minutes from the Royal Palace area, with river views the whole way.

modes.title: Tuk-tuk
points: Priced per vehicle, not per person — one tuk-tuk takes 2–4 people plus luggage.
Flag one down and agree the fare first; you can usually talk the first quote down to 70–80%.
Confirm you are heading to the night market on Preah Sisowath Quay, so you are not dropped at a different market.

modes.title: Ride-hailing / Taxi
points: Grab and PassApp show a fixed price before you book, so there is no haggling; pay by cash or card.
Type the market name or drop a pin, which avoids any language barrier.
Demand spikes in the rain and on weekend evenings, so expect a longer wait.

modes.title: Motorbike Taxi (Moto-dop)
points: Quickest option for one person with no luggage, especially in heavy traffic.
Always agree the fare before you get on.
Protection is minimal — it comes down to your own comfort level.

modes.title: City Bus
points: Very cheap; pay cash to the conductor on board.
Most routes stop running in the evening, so there is usually nothing left by the time the market closes at 11 PM.
Plan on a tuk-tuk or a ride-hailing app for the trip back.

modes.title: Driving / Private Car
points: Riverside parking is tight at night — use a paid car park at a nearby building or hotel.
There is a temporary motorbike parking area near the Street 106 and Street 108 entrances.
A drop-off and pick-up zone sits where the main entrance meets the riverside road.

modes.title: From the Airport (KTI)
modes.from: Techo International Airport (KTI), about 20 km south of the city
modes.cost: Bus about US$0.40 · app US$10–20 · taxi US$30–40
points: Important: the old Phnom Penh International Airport (PNH, Pochentong) stopped taking scheduled traffic in September 2025. All commercial flights now use Techo International Airport (KTI) — check the airport code on your ticket.
The airport express bus is by far the cheapest at around US$0.40, but it stops often and takes much longer.
Ride-hailing is the best balance of price and comfort; for taxis, use the fixed-price counter in the arrivals hall rather than drivers who approach you.
A tuk-tuk from the new airport takes over an hour — not ideal with luggage.

modes.title: By River Boat
points: Several sunset and dinner cruises leave from piers along the riverfront, on the same stretch of bank as the market.
Booking a sunset cruise and the night market for the same evening works well — you step off the boat and walk straight in.

dropoff.title: Drop-off and meeting point
dropoff.desc: The market stretches along Sisowath Quay and has no single front gate. Ask your driver to drop you where Street 106 or Street 108 meets the riverside road; step onto the promenade and the stalls are in front of you. Ordering your ride back from the same spot is easiest.

returnNote.title: Getting back at night
returnNote.desc: The market winds down around 11 PM. Tuk-tuks usually wait near the exits, and ride-hailing apps still work. Keep phones and cameras out of sight while riding and hold bags on the side away from the road — bag-snatching from passing motorbikes does happen in Phnom Penh, and almost always while the vehicle is moving.

items.title: Sisowath Quay Riverside
items.desc: A riverside promenade for evening walks, city views, and open-air dining along the Tonle Sap.

items.title: Royal Palace Area
items.desc: Cambodia's royal compound and nearby temples showcase classic Khmer architecture.

items.title: Central Phnom Penh
items.desc: Explore the city center, including markets and streets close to the riverfront.

items.title: Remove Your Shoes
items.desc: Before stepping onto the central reed mats to eat, take off your shoes and leave them at the mat's edge — a basic sign of respect for local custom.

items.title: Cash & Currency
items.desc: Both USD and KHR are accepted. For small purchases use riel or small bills ($1/$5); change is often given in riel.

items.title: Stay Safe
items.desc: Along Sisowath Quay, keep phones and bags secure while photographing — occasional snatch theft occurs near the riverside.

items.title: Bargain Politely
items.desc: Haggling is normal at markets — keep it friendly and good-natured.

items.q: What are the opening hours of Phnom Penh Night Market?
items.a: The night market is open every Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 5:00 PM to 11:00 PM. It is closed from Monday to Thursday.

items.q: Which days is Phnom Penh Night Market open?
items.a: It opens on weekends only — Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Plan your visit around those days, as the site is empty on other evenings.

items.q: Is there an entrance fee for the night market?
items.a: No, admission to the Phnom Penh Night Market is free. You only pay for the food and goods you buy.

items.q: What can visitors buy at the night market?
items.a: Visitors can find souvenirs, clothing, handicrafts, and a range of local goods.

items.q: Is the night market suitable for tourists?
items.a: Yes, it is a relaxed, family-friendly place to experience Phnom Penh's nightlife and market culture.

facilities.title: Visitor Facilities & Services
facilities.subtitle: To help you plan your trip, here is a practical overview of infrastructure and services around the night market and its surrounding area.
facilities.disclaimer: Note: As a non-profit guide, we list only categories of nearby facilities and do not recommend specific businesses.

items.title: Restrooms (WC)
points: Inside the market: paid public toilets are available within the market area, usually for a small maintenance fee (about 1,000 KHR / US$0.25). Carry some small change and tissue.
Nearby: the public promenade along the riverfront and adjacent commercial buildings also offer restroom facilities.

items.title: Parking & Transit
points: Motorbikes / e-bikes: designated temporary parking zones near the 106th & 108th Street entrances, managed by on-site staff for a small fee.
Cars: street parking along Preah Sisowath Quay is scarce at night due to crowds. Ride-hailing or tuk-tuk is recommended; if driving, use paid lots at nearby commercial buildings or hotels.
Tuk-tuk / ride-hailing: a drop-off and pick-up zone sits at the market main gate where it meets the riverside road, for quick stop-and-go.

items.title: ATMs & Currency Exchange
points: ATMs: several banks operate 24-hour ATMs around the market and along Sisowath Quay, supporting international cards (USD / KHR).
Currency exchange: licensed exchange points along the riverside let you convert foreign currency into small US dollars or Cambodian riel (KHR).

items.title: Dining Options
points: Market food court: central and riverside stalls offer charcoal grill, Khmer fried noodles, fresh spring rolls and fruit drinks, with the signature reed-mat picnic experience.
Riverside restaurants: indoor and open-air restaurants along Preah Sisowath Quay serve Khmer cuisine, French bistros, Asian fusion and Italian.
Rooftop bars: several high-rise buildings nearby have viewing bars overlooking the Tonle Sap river and Phnom Penh skyline.

items.title: Accommodation Categories
points: River-view boutique hotels: along Sisowath Quay, within walking distance of the market, ideal for the river sunset and night view.
Budget & backpacker hostels: behind the market (around 108th, 110th and 118th Streets), affordable for independent and young travellers.
Star-rated & business hotels: 10–15 minutes’ walk (near the Royal Palace or city main roads), full facilities for families and business trips.

items.title: Supermarkets & Retail
points: 24-hour convenience stores: several around the market and the riverside main road for water, mosquito repellent, snacks and daily needs.
Compact supermarkets: a few within walking distance offer imported food, household goods and personal care products.

items.title: Gas & EV Charging
points: Gas stations: the riverside market area is a scenic, pedestrian-dense zone; car fuel stations are mainly 5–10 minutes’ drive on city main roads (e.g. Preah Norodom Blvd or Preah Monivong Blvd).

EV charging: public charging in Phnom Penh is concentrated in large commercial complexes, upscale offices and some international-brand hotel parking lots. EV drivers should check open stations in advance via a maps app.

tips.title: Sockets & Voltage
tips.desc: Cambodia uses 220V. Common plugs are two-flat-pin (Type A) or two-round-pin (Type C).

tips.title: Payment
tips.desc: Market stalls mostly take cash (USD or KHR); larger supermarkets and restaurants nearby accept cards or QR payment.

meta.title: Phnom Penh Night Market Opening Hours 2026 – Phsar Reatrey
meta.description: When Phnom Penh Night Market opens each week, how late it runs, public-holiday changes, and the best time to arrive for food and atmosphere.

opening-hours.intro: Phnom Penh Night Market (Phsar Reatrey) is not a daily market — it runs only on weekend evenings along Sisowath Quay. Plan around these days so you don't arrive to a closed riverside.

sections.heading: Weekly schedule
paragraphs: The market opens Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings, roughly 17:00–23:00.
It is closed Monday to Thursday. On those nights the riverside promenade stays open, but the stalls and food court are not set up.

sections.heading: Why weekends only
paragraphs: The weekend-only format is what gives the market its scale — hundreds of stalls fill the central plaza and the riverside strip. A weekday visit means an empty square.

sections.heading: Best time to arrive
paragraphs: Stalls start setting up around 17:00 as it cools down, but the fullest atmosphere is 19:00–21:00, when the lights are on and the crowds build.
Arrive before 19:00 if you want to browse clothing and handicrafts before the food court gets busy.

sections.heading: Public holidays
paragraphs: On Cambodian public holidays the schedule can shift — the market may open an extra night or stay closed. Treat the times above as the regular pattern and confirm locally before a holiday visit. (Schedule checked October 2026.)

items.a: Friday, Saturday and Sunday, about 17:00–23:00. Closed Monday to Thursday.

items.q: What time does it get busy?
items.a: The busiest, most atmospheric window is 19:00–21:00. Stalls begin opening from around 17:00.

items.q: Is it open on public holidays?
items.a: The regular pattern is weekend evenings, but Cambodian public holidays can change the schedule. Confirm locally before a holiday visit.

items.q: How long should I plan to stay?
items.a: Most visitors spend 1.5–2.5 hours — enough to walk the stalls, eat at the mat seating, and watch the riverside.

meta.title: Phnom Penh Night Market Food 2026 – What to Eat & Prices
meta.description: The best street food to try at Phnom Penh Night Market, rough prices in USD, the riverside food court layout, and payment tips.

food.intro: The food court beside the Tonle Sap river is the heart of the night market — rows of grills and noodle stations where you grab a tray, sit on the woven reed mats, and share a meal Khmer-style.

sections.heading: Dishes to look for
paragraphs: Sach Ko Yak — herbal grilled beef skewers with lemongrass and kaffir lime.
Lort Cha — short silver-pin noodles flash-fried with chives, egg and sweet-chilli sauce.
Num Banh Chok — Cambodia's rice-noodle fish-curry dish, also sold in the evening.
Kuy Teav — clear pork-bone noodle soup.
Sugarcane and kumquat juice — the classic way to cool off.

sections.heading: Rough prices
paragraphs: Most single dishes and snacks run about US$1–3; grilled-meat skewers and noodle bowls sit toward the lower end, seafood and larger plates a bit higher.
Fresh juice is typically under US$1. There is no cover charge to enter the food area.

sections.heading: Where to eat
paragraphs: The central plaza is laid with reed mats — buy from any stall, then slip off your shoes and sit cross-legged to eat.
Riverside restaurants and cafés along Sisowath Quay are also a short walk away if you prefer a table and a view.

sections.heading: Paying
paragraphs: Bring small USD bills and riel for small purchases. Larger stalls and nearby restaurants may take cards, ABA Pay or QR code, but cash is safest at the market itself.

items.q: Is the food safe to eat?
items.a: Stick to busy stalls with high turnover and you will eat what locals eat. The covered seating keeps most of the food area dry in light rain.
Yes — the reed mats in the central plaza are communal. Remove your shoes at the mat edge before stepping on.
Yes, noodle and vegetable dishes are common; tell the vendor no meat and they will adjust.
Cash (USD or KHR) is easiest for small buys; some stalls take QR or card, but don't rely on it.

meta.title: How to Get to Phnom Penh Night Market 2026 – Map & Directions
meta.description: Find Phnom Penh Night Market on Sisowath Quay: the map and address, tuk-tuk and ride-hailing tips, parking, and the riverside walking route.

getting-there.intro: The market stretches along Preah Sisowath Quay on the Tonle Sap riverfront, near the corner with Street 106 — a straight, well-lit walk from the Royal Palace and the riverside hotels.

sections.heading: Location & map
paragraphs: Address: Preah Sisowath Quay, Phnom Penh, Cambodia (Plus Code HWFG+JV8). It sits beside the Tonle Sap passenger pier.
There is no single gate — the stalls run along the riverside promenade, so any entrance between Street 106 and Street 108 puts you straight into the market.

sections.heading: On foot
paragraphs: From the Royal Palace area it is a flat 15–20 minute riverside walk with views the whole way. The promenade is even, lit and busy in the evening.

sections.heading: Tuk-tuk & ride-hailing
paragraphs: Tuk-tuks take about 10–20 minutes from most of central Phnom Penh for roughly US$2–4; agree the fare first.
Grab and PassApp show a fixed price before you book — about US$2–6 — with no haggling. Demand spikes on weekend evenings and in rain.

sections.heading: Driving & parking
paragraphs: Riverside street parking is tight at night. Use a paid car park at a nearby building or hotel, or get dropped at the Street 106/108 meeting point.
There is a temporary motorbike parking area near the Street 106 and 108 entrances.

sections.heading: Getting back
paragraphs: The market winds down around 23:00. Tuk-tuks usually wait near the exits and ride-hailing still works — keep bags on the side away from the road and phones out of sight while riding.

items.q: Where exactly is the night market?
items.a: Along Preah Sisowath Quay near Street 106, on the Tonle Sap riverfront in central Phnom Penh.

items.q: What is the easiest way to get there?
items.a: On foot from the riverside, or a tuk-tuk or Grab for about US$2–6 from elsewhere in the city.
Car parking is limited along the quay; use paid lots nearby or a drop-off at the Street 106/108 corner.

items.q: How do I get back to my hotel?
items.a: Tuk-tuks wait near the exits at closing time, and Grab or PassApp still work. Allow extra time on busy weekend nights.
